title: Quantum simulation of circular cluster interactions in a linear spin chain
authors: Alexander van Lomwel, Hongzheng Zhao, Florian Mintert
abstract: The preparation of ground states of Hamiltonians with symmetries that are fundamentally different than those of the underlying device is a central challenge for quantum technologies. Here, we address this challenge with an analog protocol for the iconic generalized cluster Hamiltonian with the translational symmetry resultant from periodic boundary conditions based on a magnetization-preserving interaction on a linear geometry with open boundary conditions. Our results show that this goal can be achieved in a control duration that scales only moderately with the number of spins and Hamiltonian interaction complexity.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of engineering complex quantum Hamiltonians, such as those exhibiting periodic boundary conditions, using a physical device naturally constrained to open boundary conditions. The authors develop a quantum control protocol that drives the system Hamiltonian towards the target Hamiltonian by minimizing infidelity. They show that this process is highly efficient, requiring only a modest, near-linear scaling of control time with system size.
main_problem: The central challenge is preparing ground states of Hamiltonians with symmetries fundamentally different from those of the underlying physical device, specifically achieving periodic boundary conditions (PBC) interactions on a linear geometry with open boundary conditions (OBC).
main_result: The authors demonstrate that this goal can be achieved using an analog protocol whose required control duration scales only moderately (near-linearly) with the system size, even for complex PBC targets.
method: They employ time-dependent quantum control theory, designing the evolution of a system Hamiltonian $H(t)$ to map an initial state to the target ground state by minimizing operator and ground state infidelities.
model_or_system: The system is a linear spin chain modeled by spin operators ($X_j, Y_j, Z_j$). The Hamiltonians involve nearest-neighbor interactions and target cluster interactions, which are analyzed within the framework of a Lie algebra.
key_observables: Operator infidelity ($J_{op}$), projector infidelity ($J_{proj}$), and ground state infidelity ($J_{gs}$), as well as the minimum required control duration ($gT_{min}$).
important_parameters: System size ($n$), interaction range ($\alpha$), and the control duration ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the fact that the initial Hamiltonian has product state eigenstates, and the Lie algebra generated by the system operators is polynomially scaling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scaling of operator and ground state infidelities, as well as the minimum required control duration, showing weak dependence on the interaction range $\alpha$ for both OBC and PBC cases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical problem of symmetry mismatch between target and device Hamiltonians. It then analyzes the structure of the relevant Lie algebra. Finally, it develops and applies the quantum control protocol, calculating infidelities and determining the scaling of the required control time for both OBC and PBC targets.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, scalable protocol for realizing complex, symmetry-enforced Hamiltonians (like those found in quantum simulation of correlated materials) using only local, controllable interactions, which is highly relevant for designing quantum simulators.
